output.brief: Pellacott's 2026-built VA-220 valves are the problem, not the installers or the firmware. The quality lab found that 11% of never-installed 2026 Pellacott valves leak at the seat, against about 1% of 2025 Pellacott valves and none from Durrant-Hale. Claim rates are the same for new and legacy installers and for firmware 4.1 and 4.2, and Durrant-Hale valves stay low in every group. The independent calibration visit found Pellacott's only VA-220 leak rig out of service since January, with no VA-220 test logged on any other rig. The certificate tables repeat four fixed sequences, some already in use in November 2025. The certificates therefore do not reflect real tests. That also explains the score rise: the score rewarded complete certificates, and these were not real. Do now: do not release the six held lots on fresh certificates. Quarantine 2026 Pellacott stock, withdraw dock-to-stock status, and test the stock yourselves with helium. Drop the installer remediation and chargeback plan. Open a supplier investigation, since the seal change (Corlin) and the move to Line 3 can't be told apart yet. Check other suppliers' test records, because that is unknown. Add rig-log or witnessed-test checks to scoring. Confidence is high on the main conclusion.
